protections: Component file serving: a request for /component/<component_name>/<tail> must only read files under the component root registered for that name; at the pin there is no containment check at all (lib/streamlit/components/v1/components.py:310-334).

Static frontend file serving: files under lib/streamlit/static (catch-all route) and lib/streamlit/static/assets (/assets/) are confined to their roots by tornado's inherited get_absolute_path/validate_absolute_path; Streamlit only rewrites page URLs before that inherited check (lib/streamlit/server/routes.py:45-99; lib/streamlit/server/server.py:415-435).

Media serving: /media/<id> is answered only from the in-memory file manager keyed by content hash, never from disk (lib/streamlit/server/routes.py:108-205; lib/streamlit/in_memory_file_manager.py:295-303).

Page-navigation rewriting is limited to a first URL segment that is an actual page name; all other paths fall through to the inherited tornado handler unchanged (lib/streamlit/server/routes.py:64-85).

traps.reason_to_dismiss: Only component names the app explicitly registered can be resolved, and the component root itself is chosen by trusted app code; a solver can argue the handler therefore only reaches files the app already declared, and that component names are not a real attack surface.

The URL tail is expected to be a relative asset path below the component name, and rejecting '..' segments looks sufficient; an empty first tail segment (a double slash after the component name) is easy to overlook and is not a shape a '..'-oriented check catches.

A containment check written as startswith(component_root) on the joined path appears correct because the join already begins with the root; it silently passes '..' segments (the joined path is not normalized) and sibling directories that share the root's name prefix.

The media manager only returns files it already holds in memory, so there is no filesystem traversal: a solver can reasonably dismiss /media/ as out of scope for CWE-22 even though the handler validates a caller-supplied prefix of the path rather than the exact requested name.

masking: T2/T3 are masked while T1 is unfixed: with no containment check every escape works, so the absolute-path and lexical-prefix shapes only become distinguishable once a naive containment check (the shape of the earlier patch) exists.

conflicts.what: The minimal T1 fix (reject any '..' segment or take os.path.basename of the URL tail) also blocks legitimate nested component assets such as static/js/main.js that T2's path-join/absolute-path handling must keep serving; one normalized containment check has to reject escapes while preserving nested paths.

A realpath-based guard for the resolved-vs-lexical shape (T3) rejects legitimate component roots that are symlinks (npm link / node_modules in dev), while a purely lexical guard keeps those working but still admits '..' traversal (T1).

fairness_risks: A component frontend legitimately serves nested assets (e.g. /component/<name>/static/js/main.js); a rule that allows only a single filename segment would break all custom components.
Legitimate asset filenames can contain '..' as a substring (bundler output) or percent-encoded characters; a substring rejection of '..' is over-broad and rejects valid files.
Component roots are often symlinks during development (npm link, node_modules); a realpath/commonpath rule can turn a legitimate component into a permanent 404.
Missing files must keep returning the existing 404 'read error' body (lib/streamlit/components/v1/components.py:327-331) so the frontend's component-loading fallback keeps working.
A component root may be nested under another registered root or share a name prefix; containment must be checked against the specific component's root, not a global prefix.
URL-encoded path segments and '+' in asset names must continue to resolve; encoding variants are not themselves traps and should not be added to a denylist at the cost of valid names.

design.why: The advisory-related sites T1, T2 and T3 are all at the same sink and are closed by ONE correct containment check in ComponentRequestHandler.get (normalize/resolve the joined path and require it to be the component root or a descendant, while preserving nested asset paths). Per the shared-guard rule they count as a single independent trap, so the H3b2 pair (earlier patch plus its minor follow-up) does not yield the 3-5 independent judgements a stacked task needs. T4 is a separate in-memory identity weakness at routes.py:151-177 / in_memory_file_manager.py:295-303, but it is not a filesystem traversal and its link to GHSA-8qw9-gf7w-42x5 is unconfirmed, so the candidate offers at most two independent groups.

unverified: The a_fix (80d9979d5f4a) and b_fix (bd0a8996c4c7) diffs are not present in the pinned tree: setup.py:37 reports VERSION 1.11.0 and the pin contains no traversal regression tests in StaticFileHandlerTest (lib/tests/streamlit/server_test.py:750-802) or ComponentRequestHandlerTest (lib/tests/streamlit/components_test.py:400-459), consistent with the pin predating the 1.11.1 fix. The history judgements (a_fix_leaves_b_open, b_in_code_a_wrote) rest on the advisory/commit summary 'Minor fix to previous patch for CVE-2022-35918', not on path:line evidence.

Which file the advisory report leads to (routes.py StaticFileHandler vs components.py ComponentRequestHandler) is inferred from the only HTTP-reachable filesystem sink in the pin; the distance values depend on that inference.
Python semantics used for T2 (os.path.join(root, '/etc/passwd') returns '/etc/passwd'; dot segments are not normalized by the join) are standard-library behaviour and cannot be shown by a repo line.

Tornado's StaticFileHandler.get derives Content-Type from self.absolute_path and get_absolute_path is overridden to return the raw request path (lib/streamlit/server/routes.py:173-177), so /media/<known-id>.<other-ext> would be labelled from the caller's extension; the tornado implementation is not in this repository and was not read.

T4 permits no filesystem read: in_memory_file_manager.get (lib/streamlit/in_memory_file_manager.py:295-303) either returns a held InMemoryFile or raises KeyError, so it is an identity/content-type weakness rather than CWE-22 and its tie to this advisory is unconfirmed.

The static route's containment is inherited from tornado, an upstream dependency, and is not implemented in this repository; no repo-level path traversal was found against /assets/ or the catch-all static route at the pin.
